A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same regression-based label-embedding work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and experimental and proof appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification accuracies, training times, and convergence results for JOLLE implementations on LSHTC1, DMOZ, and ODP (Table 2 and Figures 1–6).

after.justification: v3 reports original embedding comparisons, accuracy statistics, coherence analyses, and computational results on the same datasets (Tables 2–5 and Figures 1–3).

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces sampling a real Johnson-Lindenstrauss matrix with accepting an embedding matrix that may be fixed or jointly learned, including complex embeddings. Complex Gaussian and deterministic Nelson embeddings are instantiated experimentally. Squared-loss regression and nearest-embedding decoding remain the core procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate extreme multiclass classification on LSHTC1, DMOZ, and ODP. Table 1 retains identical dataset statistics. The expanded discussion of zero-shot and multilabel learning introduces no evaluated datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: WLSTS disappears from the reported comparisons, although it remains cited. PD-Sparse, PPD-Sparse, Parabel, AnnexML, and both MLP loss baselines remain. The separate runtime comparison in v3 Table 5 narrows comparator participation to PD-Sparse and PPD-Sparse.

E3.justification: v3 introduces comparisons across four embedding families, including complex and prime-dimension configurations, and removes random-forest evaluations. The reported LSHTC1 cross-entropy protocol changes from batch size 2048, 10 epochs, and decay after epoch 5 to 128, 5 epochs, and decay after epoch 3 (v1 Appendix A.3.1; v3 Appendix B.1.1).

E4.justification: v3 adds direct coherence-versus-accuracy analyses across embedding constructions on all three datasets (Figures 1–3). These substantially extend the embedding-dimension investigation in v1, while its epoch-by-epoch convergence analyses in Figures 4–6 are removed.

E5.justification: v1 reports point accuracies without corresponding run counts or uncertainty estimates. v3 Section 5.2 newly documents five randomized repetitions and reports accuracy means and standard deviations throughout Tables 2–4; an increase from a known earlier run count is not established.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive matrix/dimension results and revises retained scores. LSHTC1 Rademacher n=512 changes from 0.3052 to 0.3066 ± 0.0022. Cross-entropy changes from 0.2940 to 0.2630 ± 0.0036 under the revised training protocol, so this is not a same-setting decline. Random-forest, WLSTS, and most training-time entries disappear.

T1.justification: The high-probability JLM excess-risk bound in v1 Theorem 3 is replaced by a deterministic coherence-dependent bound for unit-norm complex embeddings in v3 Theorem 4. Matrix-coherence definitions, bound coefficients, the Massart-condition threshold, and substantial parts of the appendix derivation change; this exceeds notation or theorem renumbering.

C1.justification: v1 presents a new JLM-based classification framework. v3 centers its contribution on coherence-based analysis of existing label embedding, extending the claimed theoretical scope to fixed, learned, and auxiliary-information embeddings. Section 4.2 explicitly states that the meta-algorithm itself should not be considered novel.

C2.justification: The central dimensionality-versus-accuracy interpretation remains. v3 connects the penalty to the C−1 convex-surrogate consistency barrier and explicitly limits its experiments to fixed embeddings despite broader theoretical applicability. The earlier explanation that unavailable raw text prevents language-model integration is removed.

D1.justification: v3 specifies Gaussian-column normalization, complex Gaussian sampling, and Nelson construction conditions with r=2. It removes random-forest implementation and hyperparameter details and v1's code-access footnote. Most neural-network, elastic-net, and hardware details remain, with the LSHTC1 cross-entropy settings revised.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands substantially toward coherence constructions, surrogate calibration, and established label-embedding methods, adding works such as Welch, Nelson and Temlyakov, Ramaswamy and Agarwal, Steinwart, Akata, and Rodríguez. The earlier Allwein/ECOC-centered theoretical framing is replaced, alongside explicit acknowledgment that the basic algorithm is established.

P1.justification: The title changes from Johnson-Lindenstrauss matrices to low-coherence matrices, and the abstract, introduction, related work, and problem formulation are substantially rewritten. Related work gains dedicated subsections, computational evaluation is separated, and the proof and experimental appendices exchange order.

P2.justification: v1's combined accuracy/runtime table is replaced by three detailed dataset-specific accuracy tables and a separate computational table. Six small runtime and convergence plots are replaced by three larger coherence plots with different axes and legends. The random-forest hyperparameter table is removed.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the central contribution through explicit coherence-based assumptions and revised proofs, direct empirical investigation of coherence, and five-run uncertainty reporting where v1 supplied point estimates. It also clarifies the algorithm's relationship to prior work. These gains outweigh the loss of random-forest and convergence evidence and the omitted code-access guidance; the improvement rests on stronger justification and reporting, rather than higher scores.
